html:
A band of twelve Franciscan friars who arrived in New Spain in May 1524, three years after the fall of Tenochtitlan, to convert the Indigenous peoples to Christianity. Their leader was Martín de Valencia, and the number twelve copied the apostles of Jesus.

Hernán Cortés met them as they reached Mexico City and knelt in public to kiss their hands. The scene was meant to show Nahua lords how to treat the new holy men.

The friars spread out, learned Nahuatl and other languages, built churches and schools, and baptised people in very large numbers. They also destroyed temples and images of the old gods. One of them, Toribio de Benavente, called Motolinía ("poor one" in Nahuatl), wrote a history of the Indigenous peoples. Their work began the great conversion of central Mexico, later joined by the Dominicans and Augustinians and by the devotion to Our Lady of Guadalupe.
